JULY, 1990         Page  Reply
 How to write to us...02     -
 D.H. Phillips........03    04
 A. Barnes............06    06
 Grant Dixon..........07    09
 Phil Glover..........10    10
 Leon Oblin...........11    12
 Derek Morgan.........16    20
 Ron Smith............21    23
 Frank Harrop.........24    24
 Chris Clayton........25    25
 Leif Mortensen.......26    26
 Peter Bell...........27    27
 Bob Rutherford.......28    28
 Another Ron Smith!...29    31
 Malcolm Goodman......32    32

      HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
      ----------------------
Letters are accepted in any form
for publication in OUTLETTERS:
BASIC PRINT or DATA; handwritten
or typed copy; all wordprocessor
files (please state which!) or a
simple JOTTER program is in our
Issue 2(Disk #4).The easiest for
us to edit are Tasword 2 files
with the right margin set at 32.

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From D.H. Phillips,  BRIDGEND

My set up here is a ZX Spectrum+
128K and an older 48K rubber-key
type. These drive an Interface 1
with two Microdrives and printer
output is either a Brother M1009
full-size dot-matrix printer or
a 32-column Seikosha GP-508.

Can you please inform me if the
upgrade kit (Spectrum 48K+) is
still available as the older one
of mine could do with a new
keyboard (the keys are getting
sticky).Also,do many second-hand
Interface 1's, microdrives or
cartridges come on the market
nowadays?I checked the advert in
OUTLET 33 but the items had been
sold.

To Mr. D.H. Phillips from Brian

One of the best places to look
out for second-hand I'face 1's,
cartridges etc. is in MICROMART
(if there's a newsagent near you
that has the magazine in stock).

EEC LTD., 18-21 Misbourne House,
Chiltern Hill, Chalfont St.
Peter, Bucks, SL9 9UE (Tel: 0753
887149) offer new cartridges at
the rip-off price of `4.50 EACH!
They also do expansion packs of
Interface 1 with one or two
microdrives at `59.95 and `69.95
respectively.

W.A.V.E., 1 Buccleuch Street,
Barrow-in-Furness, Cumbria LA14
1SR (Tel: 0229 870000)advertised

the 48K to 48K + upgrade pack at
`27.60 but my info is a few
months old so you may prefer to
contact them first to check if
they still have any and if the
price is unchanged. I'm certain
there must be others with the
upgrade pack in stock and I'll
keep a look out for you over the
next few months. Meanwhile, if
anyone else knows of a supplier,
please write.
                      - Brian

From R. Barnes,  WESTBURY

I feel certain I saw recently a
review of software for creating
your own WIMP environment on the
Spectrum. Do you know of it?

No, I don't recall it. Does any-
one else? By WIMP you include
file-handling? If you just want
menu-selection then MULTICURSOR
in OUTLET 34 is ideal if you can
program in BASIC. If you want to
load/erase files etc. then the
system needs to be able to read,
display and keep track of the
catalogue of files on the system
in use. No general-purpose WIMP
system would handle files on all
systems but would be specific to
one system, e.g., +3 disc.
                       - Brian

From Grant Dixon

I note from your editorial in
No.34 that I had made a'boob' by
sending the MEGADEM program to
you.I would like to apologise to
all your readers for misleading
them. The fact is I copied the
program from the Dutch language
magazine 'Disciple Nieuwsbrief'
which I had been taking from
issue 1. The declared policy of
the magazine was that nothing
should be published unless it
was Freeware so I thought that I
would translate the text into
English and pass it on to OUTLET
readers... Very sorry if I have
offended anybody, and thanks to
the two readers who wrote and
pointed out the true state of
affairs.

Incidentally,the Disciple Nieuws
brief has ceased publication and
my contact in Holland has got
himself an Amiga 2000 with hard
drive.How are the mighty fallen!
I have a full set of 16 copies
of the magazine if anyone wishes
to refer to them but I must
emphasise that the text is in
the Dutch language.

Turning to another topic, can I
congratulate you(and Mike Haine)
on the excellent routine to do a
tabloid print-out. I am now
wondering whether it would be
possible to do a similar program
which would take any Tasword
file, re-format it to 32 columns
and print it out in this way.
          Best wishes,
             Grant Dixon

To Grant Dixon from Brian



Thanks, Grant. I have a note to
ask Mike Haine the next time I
write to ask about a Tas2 3-col
program. If you read this Mike
perhaps you'd care to comment?!

(Other readers please note that
we already have Mike's TWOCOL in
OUTLET 29.)

                - Brian

From Phil Glover, BIRMINGHAM

I like your idea of an OUTLET
compilation.In back issues,T3TO2
sounds interesting.Could it move
Tas128 files to Tas2 files?

Thanks for all your suggestions
for a future compilation. Please
note that your letter- and those
received from other readers with
ideas for compilations - will be
carefully kept and referred to
when the next OUTLET EXTRA is
put together. This may be some
time in the future however as I
just cannot cope with the extra
work!  If Tas 128 files are
"open type" then T3TO2 should be
able to convert them if they are
divided up into 20K chunks.
                       - Brian

From Leon Oblin, BELGIUM


On the Opus Discovery system,I'd
like to know precisely how to
CAT,LOAD and SAVE from m/c with-
out returning to BASIC and how
to use the parallel printer port
directly from m/c without using
any ROM routine or using BASIC.
I hope you will be able to send
me documented assembler code
about shaded dumps and anything
about using Opus from m/c.

I'd like to know how to send
subroutines if ever I can (may I
use the LERM toolkit format?)and
if they can be published. Can I
get some OUTLET routines without
buying all the back-issues?

To Leon Oblin from Brian

May I remind readers that MOST
info, ideas, help, etc. is thru'
these OUTLETTERS pages or within
OUTLET in some way so that other
readers can benefit.In your case
I've sent you a copy of Section
4 of the Opus manual (courtesy
of the SPECTRUM DISCOVERY CLUB)
giving hook code details etc. It
was not included in the original
manual but I hope to put it in a
future OUTLET. I did not have
time to study it to see if it
helps with accessing the printer
port.If not,can any other reader
help? Remember, Leon, programs
that access hardware directly
will not work on other systems
but be restricted to Opus.

I have no shaded dump assembler
listings at all. The principle
must be to have a table of data
of the various patterns you want
(e.g. 11111111, etc. for black,
00000000, etc. for white and
say, 10101010 for green), test
each attribute byte and split it
into PAPER and INK values then
test each bit in that square on
the screen line you are printing
and send the data from the table
as appropriate depending if the
bit is set or not.

If you wish to contact other
OUTLET readers directly for help
with programming or to exchange
info, etc., please write again
and ask that your full address
be shown. You can, of course,

always write for help to me or
BoB Smith about specific program
problems but this help will
usually be through OUTLETTERS in
the next issue.

You can send a routine to OUTLET
in almost any format but the
most helpful is a working demo
including the object code with a
supporting BASIC program and
info (or separate text file). If
you send the source file it can
be included in OUTLET but is
only of use to readers who have
the same assembler. You might
send it as a text file with full
comments for others to type in
and modify. I wish I could get
some sort of standard system.For
example, if we had a conversion

program that could convert all
the popular assembler listing
formats into say, Tasword 2 or,
at least, straight ASCII and
vice versa then any listings
sent to us could be published in
a standard format and everyone
could convert to their favourite
assembler format! Would anyone
like to volunteer/comment??!!...

Some earlier OUTLET programs may
be re-published in compilations
like OUTLET EXTRA 1 and you are
welcome to vote for any you'd
like to be included but it may
be a long time before the next
one is issued as I am already
overworked producing OUTLET each
month!
                       - Brian

From Derek Morgan, LANCASHIRE


Hi Ron, Brian,

Thanks for the Outlet discs and
letter. What a disappointment!!!
- Not an Error, Bug or Crash to
be found anywere. What do I get
to pick at or moan about? -
nothing! How do I get a refund
when the mag is so good? What am
I saying? GOOD??!! - It's
MEGAFANTASTIC! And what about
that CATLOADER? YES!, what about
CATLOADER? It's BRILL. Don't
just sit there, get it sent off
to MGT. Win some money, get a
prize. It's so good that MGT
must include it on their new DOS
disc.

Ron. I don't like this idea of
feeding Brian on Marmite
sandwiches to get him to do 60 -
70 hours of work a week.You will
have to be more firm with him.


Brian.I think you should keep an
eye on Ron. He's put out a con-
tract on Bob Smiff but I don't
think he'll get much for 50p. Is
it true what he says about Ron?.


Before I forget, Bob tells me
that you have a member that can
help with printer problems. Boy!
Do I have a problem or what?
Does he/she have an address or
do I write to you at the mag?

Bob Rutherford. His letter on
loading +D/Disciple snapshot
files[on the SAM] made me stop
and think (Oh that hurt). You
advertise in FORMAT but didn't
know how to load snapshot files?
A letter in FORMAT April 90 from
Nick Carthy told of a world, not
too far in the past, and of a
man called SAM.The story so far:

LOAD Rom.bin 65536 (16384) off
the MGT disc. SAVE "NMI" CODE
79982,1170. LOAD Spectrum ROM to
65536. then LOAD "NMI" CODE
(79982,1170)then POKE 65638,245,
195,40,57 then SAVE "convrom"
CODE 65536,16384.

OK!, So far so good. Now write
this little program (It's on the
disc).

10 MODE 1 : pen 15
20 LOAD "Skelt.bin" CODE 65536
30 LOAD "trans.bin" CODE 16384
40 PRINT AT 10,6; "Please load a
Snapshot disc"
50 PAUSE 60
60 PRINT AT 12,8; "Please press
a key"
70 PAUSE 0
80 DIR 1
90 INPUT "Enter the number of
the file ";A$
100 LOAD VAL A$
110 CALL 16384

This program will now load and
run +D/Disciple Snapshot files.

If you do put this program in an
issue of OUTLET, a lot of
SAM users will benefit. - Derek

To Derek Morgan from Brian

I'd already sussed out how to
load the Disciple snapshots and
wrote a little loader program.It
loads a specific snapfile so can
be named "PINBALL" or whatever
whereas yours inputs the file
name. I'll try and put both in
ADD-ENDERS in this issue.The new
MGT disk includes a loader like
yours but they put it in the
emulator as the "DISK" option.

Mike Haine of "Riverside" Welsh
Road, Offchurch, Leamington Spa,
CV33 9AQ may be able to help you
with your printer problem.

Oh well, back to the sandwich...

                     - Brian

From Ron Smith,  WATFORD

I would like to see programs of
a more serious nature for the
COUPE; fast files, spreadsheets,
diaries etc.

I am not worried about trans-
ferring Spectrum programs as I
am still using the Spectrum
having had a lead made up from
the RGB socket on my 128K to the
RGB on a monitor with another
lead with EURO connectors to SAM
and monitor and, as I have them
through two switches, all I have
to do is switch one off and the
other on and vice versa.

The monitor is an ACORN RGB
colour which is ideal for both

computers. The lead was made up
by SRS Computers of Watford and
both items were purchased there.
They are very helpful.All I took
in was the RGB socket diagrams.

Regarding the subject in OUTLET
32 by Mrs. Harvey concerning the
MINI OFFICE program, I have this
program on tape for the Spectrum
128K +2,+D and 120D printer and
have been unable to print from
the WORD PROCESSING and SPREAD
programs. The DATABASE program
works ok and prints perfectly.Is
there anything I can do to make
it print out?Could Mrs. Harvey's
program help?
              Kind Regards,

                 Ron Smith

To Ron Smith from Brian

The more serious applications
software for the SAM take longer
to develop. CATLOADER, the file-
handler is already available in
OUTLET 33 but others, like the
word processor I am developing,
will take many months as I have
had to shelve the project due to
lack of time. Still, there is a
steadily-growing flow of demos,
short routines,toolkit utilities
and the like which are all of
great interest to the average
enthusiast.

Susan Harvey's MINIPRINT is in
this month's ADD-ENDERS. It
should solve your MINI-OFFICE
printout problem.
                        - Brian

From Frank Harrop,  BRIGHTON

I have been in touch with Bruce
Gordon because of the radiation
not only from the SAM computer
but also the modulator in the
power supply. I raised with MGT
in February, 1989 at the design
stage that I hoped this would be
taken into account but it's only
recently when I drew attention
to the fact that the EEC were
considering EMC regulations
(Electro-Magnetic Compatibility)
that they appointed a firm of
consultants to advise!


Thanks Frank but I wonder what
will happen now that MGT have
gone bust?              - Brian

From Chris Clayton, CARLISLE

What is the prospect of you
producing a Swift Disc version
of OUTLET?    - Chris Clayton

A few issues ago another reader
offered to duplicate OUTLET in
SWIFTDISC M/drive emulator mode
but it would not be practical
unless there's a big demand. We
asked for SD users to write but
we haven't had any response.When
you wrote previously about what
system to buy I actually began a
reply recommending a Disciple or
+D(one of many reasons being you
could buy OUTLET) but then got
your next letter saying you had
bought a SWIFTDISC! What can I
say? Aaaaaagggghhhh!!! - Brian

From Leif Mortensen, DENMARK

Do you have the colour codes for
the LC10 colour printer or other
colour printers?

About the Spectrum hard disc
interface mentioned in COMPUTER
SHOPPER- well it can be done but
they won't seriously put a lot
of hours of work into it if they
can't sell it. Do you know of a
firm which could be interested?


I'll throw both questions open
to comments from other readers!
Thanks for the great clip art. I
might prepare a list of OUTLET
FREEWARE(you also asked for)if I
can find time...
                       - Brian

From Peter Bell,  WEST SUSSEX

How long before you come up with
your SAM word processor? I have
umpteen versions of Tasword and
I'd rather not cough up a lot
for SAM versions being an OAP.

Pressing N at the CONTENTS page
of OUTLET 32 does not bring up
info for the FIVER program but
the algebraic proof spoof.

I shall try to find time to look
at my wordprocessor again but it
may be months and do not expect
other than a very simple program
although I may add improvements
later. The "proof spoof" IS the
start of the FIVER info article.
Read on!                - Brian

From Bob Rutherford,  BOSTON

Will the Spectrum programs that
won't convert to SAM still be on
the SAM version disc of OUTLET?
[as Spectrum programs saved on
the SAM-formatted disc via
Disciple and that will load via
+D/Disciple]


The SAM discs are duplicated at
my home while our Disciple is at
Ron's and the way we run things
would make it very awkward. I
will eventually have another
Disciple and drives at my place
and I will then reconsider this
idea.I may even add the programs
that got missed if I'm in a good
mood.
                     - Brian

From: Ron Smith, LONDON N.9
[Not to be confused with the Ron
Smith of WATFORD! - B.C.]

Thanks for an enjoyable and
informative Outlet.

On reading Issue 33 I think I
found a kindred spirit in J.
Briggs of Sheffield. I, like he,
employ the Spectrum as a word
processor using mainly Tas/
utilities which I find of good
quality and ease of use. I also
use my Spectrum in conjunction
with my other hobby: shortwave
radio listening (swl). I use a
number of commercially-produced
programs to decode Morse, SSTV
and Fax radio transmissions,with
some success.

My main interest is Slow Scan TV
in which still pictures are
transmitted in digital form
across the world taking either
8, 16, 32, 48 or 96 seconds to
produce in either grey scale or
colour. I cannot yet decode
colour.

If you would like me to write a
short article about SSTV to be
included in a later issue of
Outlet I would be only to
pleased to do so. It could be
complimented by, perhaps, a
letter from J. Briggs on FAX
which would be of great interest
to me as I have had no success
in that field though I have a
commercially-produced program
for decoding FAX.

My setup is Spectrum+3, Amstrad
3160 printer, MGT 3.5 Disc
drive, Alphacom 32 printer and
many other little helpers and I
am 60 this June.

My first interest in computers
came with the introduction of
the ZX81 which my wife purchased
for my sons through the original
mail-order offer and the rest is
history.

Best wishes to you both and to
Alan Oxberry who first intro-
duced me to OUTLET.
                     - MIFF
Thanks, Miff. Yes I'd be happy
to publish an article on SSTV
and/or FAX. May I also draw your
attention to Grant Dixon's
SCANDUMP in OUTLET 17? - Brian.

         Malcolm Goodman
       17 Brookhill Avenue
         Leeds, LS17 8QA
        Tel: LEEDS 683618

I need help with the single-step
trace program I'm working on -
someone with a good,in-depth
knowledge of the Spectrum ROM
would be the ideal person.

I've done a lot of spadework but
putting it all together is where
I'm thinking too clearly [sic] I
believe the idea is valid but I
think an extra set of eyes might
be able to tell if I'm wasting
my time.

Anyone wishing to help please
contact Malcolm direct.
                        - Brian.

Hi Ron, Brian,

Bob Rutherford. His letter on loading +D/Disciple snapshot files[on the SAM] made me stop and think (Oh that hurt). You advertise in FORMAT but didn't know how to load snapshot files? A letter in FORMAT April 90 from Nick Carthy told of a world, not too far in the past, and of a man called SAM.The story so far:

LOAD Rom.bin 65536 (16384) off the MGT disc. SAVE "NMI" CODE 79982,1170. LOAD Spectrum ROM to 65536. then LOAD "NMI" CODE (79982,1170)then POKE 65638,245, 195,40,57 then SAVE "convrom" CODE 65536,16384.

OK!, So far so good. Now write this little program (It's on the disc).

10 MODE 1 : pen 15 20 LOAD "Skelt.bin" CODE 65536 30 LOAD "trans.bin" CODE 16384 40 PRINT AT 10,6; "Please load a Snapshot disc" 50 PAUSE 60 60 PRINT AT 12,8; "Please press a key" 70 PAUSE 0 80 DIR 1 90 INPUT "Enter the number of the file ";A$ 100 LOAD VAL A$ 110 CALL 16384

This program will now load and run +D/Disciple Snapshot files.

If you do put this program in an issue of OUTLET, a lot of SAM users will benefit. - Derek

To Derek Morgan from Brian

I'd already sussed out how to load the Disciple snapshots and wrote a little loader program.It loads a specific snapfile so can be named "PINBALL" or whatever whereas yours inputs the file name. I'll try and put both in ADD-ENDERS in this issue.The new MGT disk includes a loader like yours but they put it in the emulator as the "DISK" option.

Mike Haine of "Riverside" Welsh Road, Offchurch, Leamington Spa, CV33 9AQ may be able to help you with your printer problem.

Oh well, back to the sandwich...

- Brian

From Ron Smith,  WATFORD

I would like to see programs of a more serious nature for the COUPE; fast files, spreadsheets, diaries etc.

I am not worried about trans- ferring Spectrum programs as I am still using the Spectrum having had a lead made up from the RGB socket on my 128K to the RGB on a monitor with another lead with EURO connectors to SAM and monitor and, as I have them through two switches, all I have to do is switch one off and the other on and vice versa.

The monitor is an ACORN RGB colour which is ideal for both

computers. The lead was made up by SRS Computers of Watford and both items were purchased there. They are very helpful.All I took in was the RGB socket diagrams.

Regarding the subject in OUTLET 32 by Mrs. Harvey concerning the MINI OFFICE program, I have this program on tape for the Spectrum 128K +2,+D and 120D printer and have been unable to print from the WORD PROCESSING and SPREAD programs. The DATABASE program works ok and prints perfectly.Is there anything I can do to make it print out?Could Mrs. Harvey's program help? Kind Regards,

Ron Smith

To Ron Smith from Brian

The more serious applications software for the SAM take longer to develop. CATLOADER, the file- handler is already available in OUTLET 33 but others, like the word processor I am developing, will take many months as I have had to shelve the project due to lack of time. Still, there is a steadily-growing flow of demos, short routines,toolkit utilities and the like which are all of great interest to the average enthusiast.

Susan Harvey's MINIPRINT is in this month's ADD-ENDERS. It should solve your MINI-OFFICE printout problem.

```text
                        - Brian
```

From Frank Harrop,  BRIGHTON

I have been in touch with Bruce Gordon because of the radiation not only from the SAM computer but also the modulator in the power supply. I raised with MGT in February, 1989 at the design stage that I hoped this would be taken into account but it's only recently when I drew attention to the fact that the EEC were considering EMC regulations (Electro-Magnetic Compatibility) that they appointed a firm of consultants to advise!

Thanks Frank but I wonder what will happen now that MGT have gone bust?              - Brian

From Chris Clayton, CARLISLE

What is the prospect of you producing a Swift Disc version of OUTLET?    - Chris Clayton

A few issues ago another reader offered to duplicate OUTLET in SWIFTDISC M/drive emulator mode but it would not be practical unless there's a big demand. We asked for SD users to write but we haven't had any response.When you wrote previously about what system to buy I actually began a reply recommending a Disciple or +D(one of many reasons being you could buy OUTLET) but then got your next letter saying you had bought a SWIFTDISC! What can I say? Aaaaaagggghhhh!!! - Brian

From Leif Mortensen, DENMARK

Do you have the colour codes for the LC10 colour printer or other colour printers?

About the Spectrum hard disc interface mentioned in COMPUTER SHOPPER- well it can be done but they won't seriously put a lot of hours of work into it if they can't sell it. Do you know of a firm which could be interested?

I'll throw both questions open to comments from other readers! Thanks for the great clip art. I might prepare a list of OUTLET FREEWARE(you also asked for)if I can find time...

```text
                       - Brian
```

From Peter Bell,  WEST SUSSEX

How long before you come up with your SAM word processor? I have umpteen versions of Tasword and I'd rather not cough up a lot for SAM versions being an OAP.

Pressing N at the CONTENTS page of OUTLET 32 does not bring up info for the FIVER program but the algebraic proof spoof.

I shall try to find time to look at my wordprocessor again but it may be months and do not expect other than a very simple program although I may add improvements later. The "proof spoof" IS the start of the FIVER info article. Read on!                - Brian

From Bob Rutherford,  BOSTON

Will the Spectrum programs that won't convert to SAM still be on the SAM version disc of OUTLET? [as Spectrum programs saved on the SAM-formatted disc via Disciple and that will load via +D/Disciple]

The SAM discs are duplicated at my home while our Disciple is at Ron's and the way we run things would make it very awkward. From: Ron Smith, LONDON N.9 [Not to be confused with the Ron Smith of WATFORD! - B.C.]

Thanks for an enjoyable and informative Outlet.

On reading Issue 33 I think I found a kindred spirit in J. Briggs of Sheffield. I, like he, employ the Spectrum as a word processor using mainly Tas/ utilities which I find of good quality and ease of use. I also use my Spectrum in conjunction with my other hobby: shortwave radio listening (swl). I use a number of commercially-produced programs to decode Morse, SSTV and Fax radio transmissions,with some success.

My main interest is Slow Scan TV in which still pictures are transmitted in digital form across the world taking either 8, 16, 32, 48 or 96 seconds to produce in either grey scale or colour. I cannot yet decode colour.

I need help with the single-step trace program I'm working on - someone with a good,in-depth knowledge of the Spectrum ROM would be the ideal person.

I've done a lot of spadework but putting it all together is where I'm thinking too clearly [sic] I believe the idea is valid but I think an extra set of eyes might be able to tell if I'm wasting my time.

Anyone wishing to help please contact Malcolm direct.

                        - Brian.

### HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET

Письма для публикации в OUTLETTERS принимаются в любом виде: бейсиковский PRINT или DATA; рукописный текст или машинописная копия; файлы любых текстовых процессоров (пожалуйста, указывайте, каких именно!) или простая программа JOTTER из нашего Выпуска 2 (Disk #4). Проще всего нам редактировать файлы Tasword 2 с правым полем, установленным на 32.

Пожалуйста, укажите, если в вашем письме есть фрагменты, которые вы не хотите публиковать, но мы в любом случае действуем на свое усмотрение. Письма также могут редактироваться для ясности и сокращения... Пожалуйста, напишите, если вы не против прямой переписки с другими читателями OUTLET, и мы опубликуем ваш полный адрес.

---

**От: D.H. Phillips, BRIDGEND**

Мой сетап состоит из ZX Spectrum+ 128K и более старой 48K «резинки». К ним подключен Interface 1 с двумя Microdrive, а вывод на печать идет либо на полноразмерный матричный принтер Brother M1009, либо на 32-колоночный Seikosha GP-508.

Не могли бы вы подсказать, продается ли еще апгрейд-кит (Spectrum 48K+), так как моему старичку не помешала бы новая клавиатура (клавиши начинают залипать). Кроме того, много ли сейчас на вторичном рынке б/у Interface 1, микродрайвов или картриджей? Я проверял объявление в OUTLET 33, но все уже было распродано.

**Мистеру D.H. Phillips от Brian**

Одно из лучших мест для поиска б/у Interface 1, картриджей и т.д. — это журнал MICROMART (если поблизости есть газетный киоск, где он продается).

EEC LTD., 18-21 Misbourne House, Chiltern Hill, Chalfont St. Peter, Bucks, SL9 9UE (Тел: 0753 887149) предлагают новые картриджи по грабительской цене £4.50 ШТУКА! У них также есть комплекты расширения из Interface 1 с одним или двумя микродрайвами по £59.95 и £69.95 соответственно.

W.A.V.E., 1 Buccleuch Street, Barrow-in-Furness, Cumbria LA14 1SR (Тел: 0229 870000) рекламировали набор обновления с 48K до 48K+ за £27.60, но моим данным уже несколько месяцев, так что лучше сначала свяжитесь с ними и уточните наличие и актуальность цены. Я уверен, что найдутся и другие продавцы с такими наборами на складе, и я присмотрю для вас варианты в ближайшие месяцы. Тем временем, если кто-то из читателей знает поставщика — напишите.
— Brian

---

**От: R. Barnes, WESTBURY**

Кажется, недавно я видел обзор софта для создания собственной WIMP-среды на Спектруме. Вы о ней слышали?

**Ответ:**
Нет, не припомню. Кто-нибудь еще знает? Под WIMP вы подразумеваете и работу с файлами? Если вам просто нужен выбор из меню, то MULTICURSOR из OUTLET 34 идеален, если вы умеете программировать на Бейсике. Если же вам нужно загружать/удалять файлы и т.д., системе потребуется уметь читать, отображать и отслеживать каталог файлов используемой дисковой системы. Никакая универсальная WIMP-система не сможет работать с файлами на абсолютно всех платформах — она должна быть "заточена" под конкретную систему, например, диски +3.
— Brian

---

**От: Grant Dixon**

Судя по вашей колонке редактора в №34, я сел в лужу, прислав вам программу MEGADEM. Я хотел бы извиниться перед всеми читателями за то, что ввел их в заблуждение. Дело в том, что я скопировал программу из голландского журнала 'Disciple Nieuwsbrief', который выписывал с первого номера. Заявленной политикой журнала было публиковать только Freeware, поэтому я подумал, что переведу текст на английский и поделюсь с читателями OUTLET... Очень жаль, если я кого-то задел, и спасибо двум читателям, которые написали и указали на истинное положение дел.

К слову, Disciple Nieuwsbrief закрылся, а мой голландский контакт обзавелся Amiga 2000 с жестким диском. Как пали сильные! У меня есть полный комплект из 16 номеров журнала, если кому-то понадобится, но подчеркиваю: текст на голландском языке.

Переходя к другой теме: могу ли я поздравить вас (и Mike Haine) с великолепной подпрограммой для газетной верстки на печати. Мне вот интересно, возможно ли сделать аналогичную программу, которая брала бы любой файл Tasword, форматировала его в 32 колонки и распечатывала таким способом.
С наилучшими пожеланиями,
Grant Dixon

**Grant Dixon от Brian**

Спасибо, Grant. Я сделал себе пометку спросить у Mike Haine в следующем письме насчет программы 3-колоночной печати для Tas2. Если ты читаешь это, Mike, может, прокомментируешь?!

(Другим читателям напоминаем, что у нас уже выходила программа Mike — TWOCOL в OUTLET 29.)
— Brian

---

**От: Phil Glover, BIRMINGHAM**

Мне нравится ваша идея сборника OUTLET. В старых номерах программа T3TO2 звучит интересно. Сможет ли она конвертировать файлы Tas128 в файлы Tas2?

**Ответ:**
Спасибо за все предложения насчет будущего сборника. Пожалуйста, имейте в виду, что ваше письмо — как и письма других читателей с идеями для сборников — будет бережно сохранено, и мы обратимся к нему при подготовке следующего OUTLET EXTRA. Это может произойти нескоро, так как я просто не справляюсь с дополнительной нагрузкой! Если файлы Tas 128 относятся к "open type", то T3TO2 должна справиться с их конвертацией, если предварительно разбить их на куски по 20K.
— Brian

---

**От: Leon Oblin, BELGIUM**

Для системы Opus Discovery я хотел бы точно узнать, как делать CAT, LOAD и SAVE в машинных кодах без возврата в Бейсик, а также как обращаться к параллельному порту принтера напрямую из кодов, минуя вызовы ROM или Бейсик. Надеюсь, вы сможете прислать мне ассемблерный код с комментариями по поводу полутонового дампа экрана (shaded dumps) и вообще по работе с Opus из машинного кода.

Еще я хотел бы узнать, как присылать подпрограммы, если у меня получится (можно ли использовать формат тулкита LERM?), и публикуются ли они. Могу ли я получить некоторые программы из OUTLET, не покупая все старые номера?

**Leon Oblin от Brian**

Напоминаю читателям, что БОЛЬШАЯ ЧАСТЬ информации, идей, помощи и т.д. распространяется через страницы OUTLETTERS или в самом OUTLET, чтобы все читатели могли извлечь пользу. В вашем случае я выслал вам копию Раздела 4 руководства к Opus (любезно предоставленного SPECTRUM DISCOVERY CLUB) с подробным описанием hook-кодов и прочего. В оригинальное руководство он не входил, но я надеюсь опубликовать его в одном из следующих выпусков OUTLET. У меня не было времени изучить его и проверить, поможет ли он с доступом к порту принтера. Если нет — может ли кто-то из читателей помочь? Помните, Leon: программы, напрямую обращающиеся к «железу», не будут работать на других системах и останутся привязаны только к Opus.

Ассемблерных листингов полутонового дампа экрана у меня нет вовсе. Принцип должен быть в следующем: создать таблицу данных с нужными текстурами (например, 11111111 для черного, 00000000 для белого и, скажем, 10101010 для зеленого), проверять каждый байт атрибутов, разбивая его на значения PAPER и INK, затем проверять каждый бит в этом знакоместе на печатаемой строке экрана и отправлять данные из таблицы в зависимости от того, установлен бит или нет.

Если вы хотите связаться с другими читателями OUTLET напрямую для помощи в программировании или обмена информацией, пожалуйста, напишите снова и попросите опубликовать ваш полный адрес. Вы, конечно, всегда можете написать мне или BoB Smith по поводу конкретных проблем с программами, но ответ, как правило, выйдет в OUTLETTERS в следующем выпуске.

Присылать свои подпрограммы в OUTLET можно практически в любом формате, но полезнее всего — работающее демо, включающее объектный код с сопровождающей программой на Бейсике и пояснениями (или отдельным текстовым файлом). Если вы пришлете исходник, его можно включить в OUTLET, но он пригодится только тем читателям, у кого есть такой же ассемблер. Можно прислать текст программы с подробными комментариями, чтобы остальные могли набрать и адаптировать его. Мне бы очень хотелось прийти к какому-то стандарту. Например, если бы у нас была программа-конвертер, которая переводила бы все популярные форматы ассемблерных листингов, скажем, в Tasword 2 или хотя бы в чистый ASCII и обратно, тогда любые присланные листинги публиковались бы в едином формате, и каждый мог бы преобразовать их в формат своего любимого ассемблера! Есть желающие вызваться добровольцем / высказать мнение?!..

Некоторые ранние программы OUTLET могут быть переизданы в сборниках вроде OUTLET EXTRA 1, и вы можете проголосовать за те, которые хотели бы там увидеть, но до выхода следующего сборника может пройти много времени: я и так перегружен ежемесячным выпуском OUTLET!
— Brian

---

**От: Derek Morgan, LANCASHIRE**

Привет, Ron, Brian!

Спасибо за диски Outlet и письмо. Какое разочарование!!! Ни единой ошибки, бага или сбоя во всем номере! К чему мне теперь придираться, на что жаловаться? Не на что! Как мне теперь требовать деньги назад, раз журнал настолько хорош? Что я говорю? ХОРОШ?? Да он МЕГАФАНТАСТИЧЕН! А как насчет CATLOADER? ДА!, как вам CATLOADER? Это просто БЛЕСК. Хватит сидеть сложа руки, отправьте его в MGT. Выиграйте денег, получите приз. Он настолько крут, что MGT обязаны включить его на свой новый диск с DOS.

Ron. Мне не нравится идея кормить Brian'а сэндвичами с Мармайтом, чтобы он пахал по 60–70 часов в неделю. Тебе надо быть с ним построже.

Brian. Думаю, тебе стоит приглядывать за Ron'ом. Он заказал Bob Smiff'а, хотя вряд ли за 50 пенсов он много получит. А правда то, что он говорит про Ron'а?..

Пока не забыл: Bob говорил мне, что у вас есть человек, который помогает с проблемами по принтерам. Боже! Уж у меня-то проблем выше крыши! У него/нее есть адрес, или писать вам в редакцию?

Bob Rutherford. Его письмо о загрузке снепшотов с +D/Disciple [на SAM] заставило меня остановиться и призадуматься (ох, аж голова заболела). Вы рекламируетесь в FORMAT, но не знали, как загружать файлы снепшотов? В письме в апрельском FORMAT 90 года Nick Carthy рассказывал о мире в недалеком прошлом и о человеке по имени SAM. Краткое содержание предыдущих серий:

LOAD Rom.bin 65536 (16384) с диска MGT. SAVE "NMI" CODE 79982,1170. Загрузите Spectrum ROM по адресу 65536. Затем LOAD "NMI" CODE (79982,1170), затем POKE 65638,245, 195,40,57, затем SAVE "convrom" CODE 65536,16384.

Отлично! Пока все идет хорошо. Теперь напишите вот эту программку (она есть на диске):

```text
10 MODE 1 : pen 15
20 LOAD "Skelt.bin" CODE 65536
30 LOAD "trans.bin" CODE 16384
40 PRINT AT 10,6; "Please load a Snapshot disc"
50 PAUSE 60
60 PRINT AT 12,8; "Please press a key"
70 PAUSE 0
80 DIR 1
90 INPUT "Enter the number of the file ";A$
100 LOAD VAL A$
110 CALL 16384
```

Эта программа загрузит и запустит файлы снепшотов с +D/Disciple.

Если вы опубликуете эту программу в номере OUTLET, это принесет пользу множеству пользователей SAM.
— Derek

**Derek Morgan от Brian**

Я уже разобрался, как загружать снепшоты Disciple, и написал небольшой загрузчик. Он загружает конкретный снепшот-файл, поэтому его можно назвать "PINBALL" или как угодно, тогда как твой запрашивает имя файла. Я постараюсь поместить обе программы в ADD-ENDERS в этом номере. Новый диск MGT включает в себя загрузчик, подобный твоему, но они встроили его прямо в эмулятор под пунктом "DISK".

Mike Haine из «Riverside», Welsh Road, Offchurch, Leamington Spa, CV33 9AQ, возможно, сможет помочь вам с проблемой с принтером.

Ну ладно, вернусь к своему бутерброду...

— Brian

---

### От: Ron Smith, WATFORD

Я хотел бы видеть более серьезные программы для COUPE: быстрые картотеки, электронные таблицы, органайзеры и т.д.

Меня не беспокоит перенос программ со Спектрума, так как я до сих пор использую Spectrum.
